dimensions.name: Deductive Logic
dimensions.definition: Ability to derive valid conclusions from premises according to the formal rules of the syllogism.

dimensions.name: Systemising Index
dimensions.definition: Propensity to identify the variables of a system and the feedback rules that govern them.

dimensions.name: Bottom-up Ratio
dimensions.definition: Predominance of raw data processing before integration into global conceptual models.

dimensions.name: Working Memory
dimensions.definition: Maximum number of constraints and semantic objects manipulated in a single contextual window.

dimensions.name: Saturation Threshold
dimensions.definition: Informational load at which syntactic structure shows coherence breakdowns.

dimensions.name: Chunking Efficiency
dimensions.definition: Ability to compress complex data sets into a semantic unit without loss of meaning.

dimensions.name: Lexical Acquisition
dimensions.definition: Speed of functional integration and syntactically correct use of a new technical term.

dimensions.name: Arborescent Thinking
dimensions.definition: Ability to maintain and explore logical sub-routines without losing the thread of the root predicate.

dimensions.name: Inference Speed
dimensions.definition: Processing time required to transform incoming information into a logical conclusion.

dimensions.name: Analytical Precision
dimensions.definition: Accuracy rate in identifying the internal components of a complex system.

dimensions.name: Definitional Rigour
dimensions.definition: Tendency to demand or provide strict definitions to limit semantic entropy.

dimensions.name: Algorithmic Thinking
dimensions.definition: Ability to decompose a task into a finite sequence of unambiguous logical instructions.

dimensions.name: Abstraction Capacity
dimensions.definition: Faculty to isolate a logical structure from its contextual support and manipulate it in pure form.

dimensions.name: Critical Synthesis
dimensions.definition: Ability to condense a large corpus by extracting only the key vectors.

dimensions.name: Selective Attention
dimensions.definition: Ability to filter irrelevant variables during a high information-density task.

dimensions.name: Probabilistic Evaluation
dimensions.definition: Tendency to quantify uncertainty rather than use binary judgements.

dimensions.name: Mental Spatialisation
dimensions.definition: Ability to model structures (hierarchies, networks) as topological objects.

dimensions.name: Cognitive Vigilance
dimensions.definition: Sustained high-level error detection across long exchange sequences.

dimensions.name: Reasoning Fluency
dimensions.definition: Ability to chain logical steps without repetition or semantic stagnation.

dimensions.name: Abductive Reasoning
dimensions.definition: Ability to identify the most probable explanation from fragmented observations.

dimensions.name: Cognitive Empathy
dimensions.definition: Logical modelling of the mental states and intentions of others (without affective resonance).

dimensions.name: Affective Empathy
dimensions.definition: Capacity for involuntary synchronisation with the emotional states of others.

dimensions.name: Masking Index
dimensions.definition: Gap between spontaneous cognitive style and adoption of neurotypical social conventions.

dimensions.name: Intent Attribution
dimensions.definition: Ability to discriminate between a system error and a deliberate intention from the interlocutor.

dimensions.name: Other-Prediction
dimensions.definition: Ability to anticipate the interlocutor's comprehension breakpoints.

dimensions.name: Hallucination Resilience
dimensions.definition: Immunity to false data presented confidently by the interlocutor.

dimensions.name: Technical Chameleoning
dimensions.definition: Adoption of optimal linguistic structures for the target system to maximise efficiency.

dimensions.name: Relational Neutrality
dimensions.definition: Absence of emotional influence markers in the structure of requests.

dimensions.name: Implicit Decoding
dimensions.definition: Ability to extract unformulated information from context.

dimensions.name: Neutral Assertiveness
dimensions.definition: Expression of limits or demands without recourse to aggression or compliance.

dimensions.name: Logical Cooperation
dimensions.definition: Tendency to collaborate based on mutual optimisation rather than social bond.

dimensions.name: Social Flexibility
dimensions.definition: Ability to adjust the level of formalism based on interlocutor feedback.

dimensions.name: Informational Density
dimensions.definition: Ratio [Semantic Units / Word Count]; measure of raw conciseness.

dimensions.name: Anaphoric Stability
dimensions.definition: Precision in maintaining reference links between pronouns and their antecedents.

dimensions.name: Non-Redundancy
dimensions.definition: Rate of new information per textual segment; absence of repetition.

dimensions.name: Literality Index
dimensions.definition: Adherence to the primary meaning of terms; rejection of metaphor and ambiguity.

dimensions.name: Quantifier Usage
dimensions.definition: Relative frequency of universal vs existential logical operators.

dimensions.name: Syntactic Complexity
dimensions.definition: Average number of subordinate clauses per sentence.

dimensions.name: Lexical Purity
dimensions.definition: Use of domain-specific terms to the exclusion of vague synonyms.

dimensions.name: Narrative Fluency
dimensions.definition: Coherence of the argumentative flow from introduction to conclusion.

dimensions.name: Imperative Hierarchy
dimensions.definition: Priority ordering of principles (e.g. Truth > Security) in dilemma situations.

dimensions.name: Intellectual Rectitude
dimensions.definition: Speed of abandonment of a hypothesis upon proof of its invalidity.

dimensions.name: Principle Stability
dimensions.definition: Resistance of core axioms to attempts at emotional persuasion.

dimensions.name: Ambiguity Tolerance
dimensions.definition: Ability to process unclassified data without forcing premature categorisation.

dimensions.name: Process Priority
dimensions.definition: Valuing the validity of the reasoning method over the final result.

dimensions.name: Epistemic Sovereignty
dimensions.definition: Maintaining one's own conclusions in the face of unproven contradictory consensus.

dimensions.name: Moral Consistency
dimensions.definition: Absence of contradictions in value judgements over time.

dimensions.name: Cognitive Friction
dimensions.definition: Energetic and temporal cost of switching between two types of cognitive tasks.

dimensions.name: Recovery Entropy
dimensions.definition: Time required to return to nominal precision after a disruption.

dimensions.name: Pattern Inertia
dimensions.definition: Tendency to repeat a thought structure after its usefulness has ceased.

dimensions.name: Informational Hygiene
dimensions.definition: Efficiency of filtering "noise" stimuli before processing.

dimensions.name: Self-Frame Generation
dimensions.definition: Ability to define one's own processing rules without external instruction.

dimensions.name: Systemic Resonance
dimensions.definition: Ability to detect a general law from a small data sample.

dimensions.name: Heuristic Repair
dimensions.definition: Ability to generate a novel decision rule when faced with an unknown situation.

dimensions.name: Degradation Gradient
dimensions.definition: Morphology of performance decline (linear vs sharp drop).

dimensions.name: Camouflage Index
dimensions.definition: Score measuring social normalisation effort.

dimensions.name: Logical Overload
dimensions.definition: Saturation threshold specific to unstructured data.

dimensions.name: Cognitive Agency
dimensions.definition: Strength of imposition of the internal frame onto the external environment.

dimensions.name: Synchronization Efficiency
dimensions.definition: Ease of synchronizing information and replies across concurrent interaction steps.

dimensions.name: Attention Reallocation
dimensions.definition: How readily attention moves between different cognitive subdomains.

dimensions.name: Environmental Adaptivity
dimensions.definition: Capacity to adjust strategy to changing environmental signals.

dimensions.name: Cognitive Redundancy
dimensions.definition: Degree of maintaining alternative reasoning chains for robustness.

dimensions.name: Temporal Consistency
dimensions.definition: Stability and consistency of reasoning across successive operations.

dimensions.name: Autonomy Index
dimensions.definition: Ability to make decisions and operate with limited external guidance.

dimensions.name: Flow Sustainability
dimensions.definition: Sustained engagement with complex work over extended periods.

dimensions.name: Information Bottleneck
dimensions.definition: Identification of critical information or execution paths that constrain progress.

dimensions.name: Noise Resilience
dimensions.definition: Preservation of useful reasoning quality under irrelevant or stochastic interference.

dimensions.name: Meta-Flow Awareness
dimensions.definition: Detection and monitoring of drift or bias in the current reasoning process.

dimensions.name: Reflective Alignment
dimensions.definition: Revision of internal models in response to observed outcomes.

dimensions.name: Decision Calibration
dimensions.definition: Calibration of decisions and thresholds when new evidence arrives.

dimensions.name: Resource Optimization
dimensions.definition: Allocation of cognitive resources among competing constraints.

dimensions.name: Outcome Consistency
dimensions.definition: Consistency of conclusions across domains and subsequent checks.

dimensions.name: Cognitive Sovereignty
dimensions.definition: Ability to retain self-directed cognitive control in mediated systems.

dimensions.name: Symbol-to-meaning conversion
dimensions.definition: Ability to reconstruct the meaning of an unfamiliar symbolic expression; measure separately for each notation, domain, and direction of conversion.
dimensions.initial_context: mathematical notation vs natural language vs program code

dimensions.name: Semantic anchoring before formalism
dimensions.definition: Extent to which a new symbolic representation becomes intelligible after concrete mechanisms, expanded examples, and explanatory scaffolding.

dimensions.name: Context-dependent compression tolerance
dimensions.definition: Difference between efficient compression of already-understood ideas and the need for explicit semantic bridges when conventions are unfamiliar.

dimensions.name: Mechanistic execution optimization
dimensions.definition: Capacity to investigate and improve instruction dispatch, branching, memory layout, stack accesses, and critical execution paths through concrete implementation.

dimensions.name: Cross-scale architectural navigation
dimensions.definition: Ability to connect system-level abstractions to primitive implementation mechanisms and move between those levels when needed.

dimensions.name: Generalization drive
dimensions.definition: Tendency to expand a local design into a reusable general architecture, including cases where this increases time to an executable result.

dimensions.name: Operational closure threshold
dimensions.definition: Conditions under which exploratory/generalizing work is bounded and converted into a finished, observable, tested result.
